notes.summary: Direct, presentation-independent order bijections between the actual H, CPSH and PSH spaces for arbitrary Reeb fields, including irrational fields, with explicit pointwise bounds and decreasing-net continuity. Finite-energy preservation and energy differentiation are not established.
notes.detailedSummary: Finite homogeneous generators give degree ratios l≤qζ/qξ≤u and δ=max|log(qζ/qξ)| uniformly over all occurring weights. Define transport by the unique zero of the original potential along a ζ orbit, rather than by an unexplained change of FS presentation. This yields order bijections, inverse and cocycle identities, and an actual passage through continuous and decreasing psh limits. For nonpositive potentials, e^δφ≤Cξζφ≤e^−δφ; fixed-measure integrals satisfy a corresponding domination bound. Homogeneous tests are dense only on the fixed invariant carrier X0^T. The transport is nonlinear and does not commute with constants or identify energies.
notes.text:
Let X=Spec R be the stated normal affine cone, with homogeneous algebra generators g_i of the vertex ideal, weights β_i, and qη(α)=〈η,α〉. Set l=min_i qζ(β_i)/qξ(β_i), u=max_i qζ(β_i)/qξ(β_i), and δ=max_i |log(qζ(β_i)/qξ(β_i))|. Every occurring nonzero weight is a nonnegative integer sum of generator weights: express a nonzero homogeneous element as a homogeneous polynomial and select a surviving monomial. Its degree ratio is a convex combination of the generator ratios. Therefore lqξ(α)≤qζ(α)≤uqξ(α), with e^−δ≤l≤u≤e^δ. On a compact Reeb set K, δ≤(max_i||β_i||*/a_K)||ξ−ζ||, where a_K=min_{η∈K,i}qη(β_i)>0. These constants are independent of potential presentations and rational denominators.

Use the actual definitions of H, CPSH and PSH from Yueqiao Wu 2406.13684v1: homogeneous finite maxima, their local uniform closure, and nontrivial decreasing CPSH limits. All these functions factor through torification r_T(v)(f)=min_α v(f_α). Work first on invariant punctured semivaluations. The torus action aη(t) adds tqη(α) to v(f_α). It is a continuous Gauss semivaluation action, invertible on invariant points. Multiplicativity follows by choosing an additive total order on the character lattice and selecting the extreme component among components of least translated value in each factor; their extreme product contribution cannot cancel. Define ρη=max_i −v(g_i)/qη(β_i). The ultrametric inequality and degree-weighted monomial averages show this equals the homogeneous supremum defining the reference potential. The unique time taking v to the fixed carrier S=X0^T is ρη(v), since min_i(v(g_i)+tqη(β_i)) has that unique zero.

For φ∈H(ξ), each term of φ(aζ(t)v) has slope in [−u,−l]. Hence for t≥0,
φ(v)−ut≤φ(aζ(t)v)≤φ(v)−lt.
These inequalities pass through local uniform and decreasing pointwise limits. Consequently a PSH potential is either finite and strictly decreasing Lipschitz along a ζ orbit, with opposite infinite endpoint limits, or identically −∞ on that orbit.

Define Cξζφ(v) as the unique t with φ(aζ(t)v)=0 when φ(v) is finite, and −∞ otherwise. This uses the actual function. For φ=max_j(−v(f_j)+λ_j)/qξ(α_j), its root is exactly max_j(−v(f_j)+λ_j)/qζ(α_j): at that time all translated numerators are nonpositive and one is zero. Thus equal FS functions have equal transported functions regardless of presentation.

For CPSH membership, approximate φ locally uniformly by FS functions. On a compact invariant set, root bounds keep the roots in a bounded interval. Its translations through that interval form a compact set. An ε error there changes roots by at most ε/l. The transported FS functions therefore converge locally uniformly to Cξζφ. Compact sets on the full punctured cone reduce to their compact torifications.

For φ_j decreasing to φ, transported roots decrease. At a finite point put t=Cξζφ(v). Then 0≤Cξζφ_j(v)−t≤φ_j(aζ(t)v)/l→0. At a point where φ(v)=−∞, the bounds min(φ_j(v)/l,φ_j(v)/u)≤Cξζφ_j(v)≤max(φ_j(v)/l,φ_j(v)/u) force the root limit to −∞. A finite point of φ remains finite after transport, so this is an actual nontrivial PSH(ζ) limit.

Transport preserves the zero set and finite-value locus. Since φ(aξ(t)v)=φ(v)−t, transport back recovers φ. The same argument on a third Reeb orbit gives CζθCξζ=Cξθ. Function order gives root order. This proves order bijections on H, CPSH and PSH, commuting with decreasing nets.

On S, semivaluations are nonnegative on R; a negative value in the vertex ideal would force its ideal value to −∞ by taking powers. Every FS potential has its maximum at the trivial semivaluation, and this passes to continuous and decreasing limits. Its value there is finite for any nontrivial psh potential, by the slice description. Thus normalization sup_S φ=φ(v_triv)=0 is legitimate and preserved. For any φ≤0 on S, the root bounds give φ/l≤Cξζφ≤φ/u, hence e^δφ≤Cξζφ≤e^−δφ. At finite points, |Cξζφ−φ|≤(e^δ−1)(−φ). For a fixed Radon probability μ on S and φ∈L1(μ), this proves transported integrability and |∫Cξζφ dμ−∫φ dμ|≤(e^δ−1)∫−φ dμ. This does not cover moving MA measures.

Carrier density requires the correct quantifier. On A2 with its full diagonal torus, ord_{x−y} and v_triv lie in X0, agree on every nonzero monomial, and have the same torification, but differ on x−y. Homogeneous tests cannot separate full-link points. Distinct points of S do differ on a homogeneous f; max(−v(f)/qξ(wt f),−L), for sufficiently large L, separates them, including infinite values. This is the restriction of max(−v(f)/qξ(wt f),ρξ−L)−ρξ. Differences of CPSH functions form a real lattice containing constants: same-ray sums follow by common-degree products for rational fields and the uniform approximation bounds for irrational fields. For u=a(φ−ψ), v=b(θ−χ), use max(u,v)=max(aφ+bχ,bθ+aψ)−(aψ+bχ). Lattice Stone–Weierstrass gives density in C(S), not C(X0).

The transport does not commute with constants. For ξ=(1,1), ζ=(1,2) on A2, transport of ρξ+c is max(log|x|+c,(log|y|+c)/2). For c>0 it takes c at v_triv and c/2 at v(x)>c,v(y)=0. No energy or MA functoriality is inferred.

Full arguments are retained in P13.1-argument.md, Sections 1–4, and P13.1-paper.tex. Rerun the finite diagnostics with python3 check_partial_results.py. They checked 63 exact rational root/sandwich cases and 252 slope instances; these finite observations do not verify the infinite-domain draft proofs.

notes.summary: Uniform quantitative comparison of actual nonnegative cumulative-filtration S invariants, including irrational Reeb fields. An exact constant-shift example exposes an incompatible E=S normalization in the supplied Wu2022 text; relevant energy-sign corrections are derived directly.
notes.detailedSummary: For a nonnegative, multiplicative, T-invariant, linearly bounded filtration with the supplied jumping-average limit, graded subspace inclusions prove e^−(2n+1)δ Sξ≤Sζ≤e^(2n+1)δ Sξ, independently of the filtration and rational denominators. This is not a completed-potential energy estimate. On A2, the total-degree filtration has S_m=2/3 for every positive integer m, while its induced constant-shift potential has probability-normalized energy 1. The printed E=S identity cannot be used unchanged. Concavity and a repaired mixed-integral estimate also correct relevant printed sign chains.
notes.text:
Use the degree constants proved in n1. Let F be an actual nonnegative, multiplicative, T-invariant, linearly bounded filtration as in Yueqiao Wu 2106.13395v2, Definition 3.5. Define Rη(m)=⊕_{qη(α)≤m}Rα, Nη(m)=dim Rη(m), and Aη(m) as the sum of filtration jumping numbers. The supplied Theorem 3.12 and Corollary 3.13 give Sη=lim Aη(m)/(mNη(m)); Vη=lim n!Nη(m)/m^n is the actual cone volume. Integer limits extend to real cutoffs by floor/ceiling and monotonicity. Finite-dimensional filtered linear algebra gives Aη(m)=∫_0^∞dim F^tRη(m)dt, so A is monotone under the graded inclusions below.

The degree bounds give Rξ(m/u)⊂Rζ(m)⊂Rξ(m/l). Taking dimensions and jumping sums, then limits, yields
u^−n Vξ≤Vζ≤l^−n Vξ,
u^−(n+1) SξVξ≤SζVζ≤l^−(n+1) SξVξ.
Dividing positive volumes proves (l^n/u^(n+1))Sξ≤Sζ≤(u^n/l^(n+1))Sξ, and therefore e^−(2n+1)δ Sξ≤Sζ≤e^(2n+1)δ Sξ. If Sξ=0, both bounds force Sζ=0. Constants are independent of F, its finite generators and rational denominators. Nonnegative jumps are essential to this proof. Signed filtrations are outside the assertion. Making jumps nonnegative by twisting with qξ does not become a constant shift after transport to ζ.

The affine-cone probability convention is MAη=vol(η)^−1 times n−1 positive potential factors and the link factor d'd''max(ρη,0). Energy has coefficient 1/n times the sum of its n normalized mixed integrals. These are the actual source operators; no formal mixed or inverse-potential object is introduced.

An exact normalization diagnostic prevents silently identifying the preceding S comparison with energy. On A2 with ξ=(1,1), let F^tR be spanned by monomials of total degree at least t. Its finite-type norm has χ(x)=χ(y)=1, inducing ρξ+1. Every normalized mixed measure in the energy formula is unchanged by this constant shift and has mass one, so Eξ(ρξ+1)=1. For every positive integer m,
N(m)=(m+1)(m+2)/2,
A(m)=Σ_{d=0}^m d(d+1)=m(m+1)(m+2)/3,
S_m=A(m)/(mN(m))=2/3.
Thus S=2/3. The supplied Wu22 Theorem 5.15, LF 1357–1372, prints E=S, incompatible with these definitions. Its Lemma 3.16(b) already prints S=n/(n+1) times the degreewise average. The factor (n+1)/n repairs the example and rational degreewise normalization; no general corrected identity is assumed here. Wu24 Proposition 7.4 explicitly uses that factor in its rational Dirac-energy statement.

For actual same-Reeb continuous psh potentials, the mixed terms in the energy-difference formula decrease from the ψ endpoint to the φ endpoint. Their average gives
∫(φ−ψ)MA(φ)≤E(φ)−E(ψ)≤∫(φ−ψ)MA(ψ).
Wu24 Proposition 7.3 at LF 1249 prints the first direction reversed. The dual tangent identity needs the displayed corrected direction. This follows directly from the positive mixed energy formula and Hodge inequality; it is not an obstacle derivative theorem.

A direct repair of the relevant Wu24 Lemma 6.4 sign chain uses normalized nonpositive FS potentials φ0,…,φ_{n−1} and τ=Σφi/n. The other n−1 energy summands are nonpositive, so ∫τMA(τ)≥nE(τ)≥−n max_i(−E(φi)). Since τ≤φ0/n and positive expansion gives MA(τ)≥((n−1)!/n^(n−1))MA(φ1,…,φ_{n−1}), multiplication by φ0≤0 yields
∫τMA(τ)≤(1/n)∫φ0MA(τ)≤((n−1)!/n^n)∫φ0MA(φ1,…,φ_{n−1}).
Consequently the last integral is at least −n^(n+1)max_i(−E(φi))/(n−1)!. This is a fixed-Reeb bound with actual positive products. It does not establish cross-Reeb finite-energy continuity.

P13.1-argument.md, Section 5, contains these proofs and exact conventions. Literal source statements and proof bodies are retained in source-extracts/source-provenance.json. Rerun python3 check_partial_results.py. It independently enumerated the degree-filtration counts for m=1,…,32; at m=32 it found N=561, A=11968, S_m=2/3. The symbolic calculation above proves the identity for all integer m; the finite enumeration is diagnostic only.

notes.summary: The new Lyuhui Wu v1 proof was inspected through Theorems 6.3, 6.5 and 7.1. Its projective envelope application remains conditional on indispensable imported proof steps. Under that explicit premise, checked rational quotient transfer and orbit transport give uniform envelope comparison for all Reeb fields.
notes.detailedSummary: Body Theorem 7.1 covers geometrically unibranch projective varieties; Theorem 6.5 first requires a countable dense subfield, and Section 7 removes that condition separately. The strict-barrier proof imports APW26b assertions whose texts are not supplied. Rational quotients are normal projective varieties with an actual ample rational polarization obtained from a divisible Veronese; residual torus invariance must be retained. Assuming the audited projective envelope premise, homogeneous approximation identifies the global envelope with the carrier envelope. The direct transport from n1 then proves ||Pξh−Pζh||∞≤2(e^δ−1)osc(h), including irrational fields, without claiming energy or finite-energy operator convergence.
notes.text:
Lyuhui Wu 2609.27610v1 is distinct from Yueqiao Wu2022/2024. The cache is arXiv-stamped 23 September 2026; no peer review or independent correctness verdict is assumed. Body Theorem 7.1, literal LF 2697–2699, states the envelope property for geometrically unibranch projective varieties over discretely or trivially valued equicharacteristic-zero fields. Completeness is the standing convention and explicit in Theorem 6.5. The trivially valued field in the problem is complete.

The actual proof was inspected. For a field admitting a countable dense subfield, Section 7 resolves singularities, applies the smooth envelope theorem upstairs, descends the usc envelope along connected geometric fibres using Proposition 2.24, and invokes Theorem 6.5. The latter, LF 1938–1959, assumes that countability hypothesis and an ample rational semipositive model datum; it uses chart potentials, Theorem 6.3, logarithmic regularization, and c↓1. The paragraph at LF 1942 does not justify its reduction of an arbitrary ample semipositive model form to a trivial embedding form.

Theorem 6.3 uses singular-locus induction, finite maps to smooth affine targets, Proposition 6.14, Lemma 6.15, Runge criteria and strict psh barriers from Lemmas 6.6–6.7. Lemma 6.6 imports APW26b Proposition 5.7 and Lemma 5.11. Lemma 3.4 imports APW26b Proposition 3.10, Proposition 3.15(3), and Theorem 5.14. These are actual proof dependencies. The bibliography at LF 2830–2833 lists APW26a/b only as Preprint (2026), without arXiv IDs; their proof texts are not among the five permitted sources.

Section 7, LF 2718–2747, removes countability by descending a PL obstacle and then each competitor to countable fields, using orthogonality, MA pushforward compatibility, positivity and domination. Over a trivial valuation, a countable dense subfield equals the whole field, so Theorem 6.5 alone cannot handle arbitrary k. The literal LF 2731 competitor quantifier must be restricted to psh PL competitors below the obstacle. The support equality at LF 2742–2743 only needs an inclusion, since the preceding statement gives a contact-support inclusion. These observations do not prove the indispensable imported assertions or base-change compatibility.

Retain the explicit premise Env: the projective envelope theorem and its necessary local imports, reference reductions, orthogonality, base-change compatibility and domination steps are valid in the stated setting. This note neither refutes nor independently establishes Env. All envelope conclusions below are conditional on it.

Check the rational application as follows. Write η=sη0, with η0 primitive integral and s>0 rational. Vη=Proj R is projective through a sufficiently divisible positive Veronese. It is normal: on D+(f), R_f is normal and its degree-zero subring is normal, since an element integral over that subring belongs to R_f and remains degree zero. Over the given algebraically closed characteristic-zero field it is geometrically normal and unibranch. No smoothness or finite quotient singularity assumption is made; general normal singularities can occur. Choose d divisible enough that L_d=O_Vη(d) is an actual ample line bundle. The rational polarization is Lη=L_d/(sd). Equivalently one can retain the Seifert/orbiline datum and its stabilizer/boundary multiplicities. They cannot be discarded by treating O(1) as an honest line bundle without passing to d. The residual torus T/Gm(η0) and its linearization remain.

The fixed-rational Wu22 Lemmas 5.11–5.12 and Proposition 5.13 identify Vη^an with the larger Gm-invariant slice X0^Gm(η0), and common-degree homogeneous FS lists with global FS metrics on Lη. Common degree is obtained by taking powers of the finitely many sections. The 1/s factor agrees with qη=sqη0. Projective dimension is n−1. Residual torification retracts this larger carrier to the fixed S=X0^T; they are not the same space.

Under Env, lift h∈C(S) to H=h∘r_T on the larger slice. Its global envelope U is continuous psh and invariant under residual T(k), since translating competitors preserves H and the reference. Convert group invariance into homogeneous approximation explicitly: uniformly approximate U by global FS metrics and take the supremum of each metric's torus translates. For a section decomposed as Σsα, sup_{t∈T(k)}|Σt^αsα|(v)=maxα|sα|(v). The upper bound is ultrametric; the lower bound follows by avoiding cancellation in the nonzero leading residue Laurent polynomial over an extension of the infinite field k. The resulting supremum is a finite homogeneous FS maximum, retains the empty common zero locus, and has the same uniform error to U. Therefore U factors through torification and descends to CPSH(η). Every cone psh competitor descends through its defining decreasing net to a global invariant competitor. Conversely U descends to a cone competitor below h. Thus Pηh=sup{φ|S:φ∈PSH(η),φ|S≤h} is the actual carrier envelope and is continuous psh for each rational η, conditionally.

Here is the quantified irrational passage using n1. Subtract sup h and put M=osc_S h, so −M≤h≤0. Every competitor can be truncated to max(φ,ρξ−M), still a competitor and now in [−M,0] on S. Set κ=e^δ−1. The n1 bound implies Cξζφ−κM is a ζ competitor below h, yielding Pξh≤Pζh+2κM. For rational ζ, its conditional envelope is itself in [−M,0]; transport it back and subtract κM to get the reverse inequality. Also ||CζξPζh−Pξh||∞≤3κM. Choose rational ζ_j→ξ. Finite-generation constants give δ_j→0, and the transported envelopes are actual CPSH(ξ) functions converging uniformly on S. Fixed-ξ equivariance gives local uniform convergence on the punctured cone. Closedness of CPSH(ξ) proves Pξh∈CPSH(ξ). The symmetric competitor argument then proves ||Pξh−Pζh||∞≤2(e^δ−1)osc h for every pair, including irrational fields. Restoring the obstacle constant uses Pη(h+c)=Pηh+c at each fixed field, not constant-equivariance of transport.

For decreasing bounded usc obstacles, decreasing envelope convergence follows by the usual order argument only when the envelopes are psh and there is a nontrivial limiting competitor: the decreasing psh limit is below the limiting obstacle and dominates every competitor. No unconditional unbounded obstacle or energy limit is claimed.

The checked application and proof are in P13.1-argument.md, Sections 6–8, and P13.1-paper.tex. Exact versions, hashes, LF ranges, literal proof bodies and limitations are in source-extracts/source-provenance.json. Rerun python3 audit_sources.py. This conditional envelope result does not prove finite-energy transport, moving-MA integration continuity, or uniform energy differentiation.

notes.text:
The retained findings n1–n3 do not solve unchanged original P13.1. The following indispensable analytic conclusions remain unproved: an estimate for Eζ(Cξζφ) for all φ∈E1(ξ), with constants independent of bounded truncation; preservation of E1 under transport; control of actual positive mixed MA through varying-Reeb approximants with uniformly integrable singular tails; a genuine cone obstacle energy extension and orthogonality theorem; and the required uniform derivative error. For example, no bound |Eξ↓(φ+tf)−Eξ(φ)−t∫_S f MAξ(φ)|≤C(K,f)t² has been established uniformly over the required finite-energy potentials and Reeb fields in a compact set. The projective envelope premise in n3 also remains conditional on indispensable unestablished imports and proof reductions.

Wu24 Theorem 6.3 is a fixed-Reeb theorem for decreasing nets with finite-energy limits at that polarization. It cannot justify two changing polarizations before finite-energy preservation is proved. The fixed-measure domination in n1 does not justify unbounded integration against moving measures. The filtration comparison in n2 is not an energy comparison on completed potential spaces.

Boucksom–Jonsson 1801.08229v4 Theorem 8.5 has a uniform O(t²) remainder on one projective variety at a fixed ample class. Its inspected proof, LF 4919–4943, uses an actual positive mixed measure at ω+εω′ and fixed mixed intersection masses. Applying it separately to differently graded rational quotients supplies no denominator-independent constants for a carrier test. Nonlinear root transport does not supply that additive positivity structure. Its Theorem 13.1 derives orthogonality using differentiation, so it cannot replace an independently justified cone transfer. Boucksom–Jonsson 2307.01697v1 requires a common test vector space, additive ordered forms, actual positive mixed products, integration by parts, Hodge negativity, orthogonality and submean properties. Those hypotheses for varying Reeb fields have not been established here. No P13.2 image or existence claim is made. The fixed carrier S=X0^T and affine-cone probability convention remain in force.
